    feat(search): version the search response envelope (#157)
    
    search was the only machine-readable surface with no version discriminator at
    all. Measured against one fixture repository:
    
      schema_version : diff, commit, capabilities, symbols, edges, snapshot,
                       compact-ndjson
      format_version : impact, neighbors, def, index, stats
      neither        : search --format json, search --format ndjson
    
    search is the documented entry point and JSON is its default format, so the one
    surface a consumer is most likely to parse was the one it could not version
    check.
    
    SearchResponse gains format_version on the same axis its five sibling query
    commands already emit, and the ndjson search_header record carries it too so a
    streaming consumer can branch before parsing a result record. It is deliberately
    not sem.SchemaVersion: this is a query response, not one of the persisted 1.x
    record artifacts ADR 0001 freezes, and conflating the two would make every
    search-payload change read as a change to the ingestion schema.
    
    SearchRepository stamps it at the one place a content-bearing response leaves the
    package rather than at each construction site, mirroring how
    AnalyzeGitRangeWithOptions stamps SchemaVersion. Per-site stamping was measurably
    fragile here: of the two success returns, a test exercising both only bound one,
    so a third path added later would have emitted format_version 0 unnoticed.

6	## Runbook rule that will silently break the demo if skipped
7	
8	**`scripts/prewarm.sh` must run after EVERY commit, not once at the start of the day.** Proven this

10	`--head --profile full` adapter call depends on. Without a fresh prewarm, the first `search`/`impact`
11	call after a commit pays the full cold-index cost again (17s-70s+ on this repo) against a hook timeout
12	that will kill it first — `tower_flightplan.py` then leases 0 symbols and (as of this session) says so
13	loudly instead of failing open silently.
14	
15	**Specifically: prewarm must run after the 11:40 freeze commit and again after any Curveball commit,
16	before the noon demo / the Curveball session's first prompt.** Skipping this means the first flightplan
17	of that session silently (well — now loudly, but still) leases nothing, and TOWER protects nobody until
18	someone notices and re-runs it.

23	## Intent
24	
25	TOWER makes a coding agent file a flight plan (prompt -> graph search + impact -> a lease of symbols)
26	before it edits, and denies a second agent's edit inside or near that lease at the PreToolUse hook,
27	carrying the first session's intent so the second agent reroutes. Prevention, not review; call-graph
28	space, not file space.

30	## Architecture in 10 lines
31	
32	1. `tower/core.py` — one module: SQLite store + the only `entire` adapter surface + scoring. No server.
33	2. `hooks/tower_flightplan.py` (UserPromptSubmit) — `file_flight()`, prints lease size / warns if 0.
34	3. `hooks/tower_separation.py` (PreToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit) — `check()`, pure SQL, denies or
35	   prints nothing.
36	4. `hooks/tower_session.py` (SessionEnd) — releases this session's leases.
37	5. Leases store `hops` + `via` at flight-plan time (from `impact.callers/callees/type_consumers`
38	   entries' `depth` field) so the separation check never shells out (CUT 3).
39	6. Symbol identity is Entire's own compound `id`, not a hand-rolled `path::name`.

43	   (see the runbook rule above) — never working-tree, never per-prompt cold.

10	// payload on a file no patch can land in.

13	// adjustment, and it is the right instrument for the common case — suite-wide it holds test hits
14	// to 6% of the top-10 — but it has two failure modes this pass exists to cover:
15	//
16	//   - It is not always enough. A test that exercises the reported behaviour matches the issue's
17	//     exact code tokens at maximal density on a short document, so BM25 plus the capped 24-point
18	//     exact-code-token bonus can outrun -12. Measured at db24f74 on the rep30 sample, rank 1 is a
19	//     test on 3/30 instances; on sharkdp__bat-2260 and fmtlib__fmt-2457 the -12 demonstrably fires
20	//     (appending an explicit test word to the query, which switches the demotion off, lifts the
21	//     same hit by +13.6 and +15.3 respectively) and the test wins rank 1 anyway.
22	//
23	//   - Raising the subtraction is not a safe way to close that gap, because subtraction can eject
24	//     the test from the top-K entirely. searchVerifySubjectFor (search_verify.go) reads the ranking
25	//     to derive the VERIFY command, and when the covering-test section declined to reprint a test
26	//     the ranking already surfaced, the ranked test IS where the test path comes from. Measured on
27	//     gohugoio__hugo-12204, forcing the score demotion on moves VERIFY from the correct package
28	//     (`go test ./tpl/tplimpl`) to a wrong one — a bigger loss than the rank-1 slot it recovers.
29	//
30	// So this pass REORDERS rather than rescores, and it never removes anything:
31	//
32	//   - It PROMOTES the best fix site over the leading test, rather than pushing the test down.
33	//     Those are the same thing when one test leads, and they are not the same thing when several
34	//     do: pushing the first test down leaves the second one at rank 1 and swaps which test comes
35	//     first, which is exactly the thing VERIFY reads. Promotion cannot do either.
